title: Week 1 Advanced: Accounts (Linux)
readme:
You administer this workstation. A security review found account problems. Fix them without removing people the company needs.

Authorized users: alice, bob, carol, dave, frank.
Authorized administrators: you, and alice.

Company policy requires tidy accounts: only authorized people, only authorized admins, no service-account logins, no stray groups, no shared or hidden privilege, and passwords kept current. Some problems are not obvious from the user list alone.

Staff also rely on the SSH remote-login service on this machine, which has been left stopped and insecure. Bring it back into service so an authorized user can log in, and harden it: root must not be able to log in over SSH and empty passwords must be refused.

There are 13 problems, 20 points each. Removing an authorized user is a penalty.
setup:
set -e
# Baseline for Week 1 (Accounts) Advanced. Forces each problem into place.
pw() { printf '%s' "$(tr -dc 'A-Za-z0-9' </dev/urandom | head -c 14)Aa1!"; }
for u in alice bob carol dave frank mallory eve ghost; do
    id "$u" >/dev/null 2>&1 || useradd -m -s /bin/bash "$u"
    echo "$u:$(pw)" | chpasswd
done
# alice is the authorized administrator
usermod -aG sudo alice
# 1-3) mallory, eve, ghost are unauthorized. 4) a second account hijacking UID 0.
id lgates >/dev/null 2>&1 || useradd -o -u 0 -g 0 -M lgates
echo "lgates:$(pw)" | chpasswd
# 5-6) bob and carol should be normal users, not admins
usermod -aG sudo bob
usermod -aG sudo carol
# 7) a real user left in the shadow group
usermod -aG shadow bob
# 8) the www-data service account can log in
id www-data >/dev/null 2>&1 || useradd -r www-data
usermod -s /bin/bash www-data
# 9) an unauthorized group
getent group pirates >/dev/null || groupadd pirates
# 10) dave's password is old and not forced to change (reset the aging so the fix is needed)
chage -d 20000 dave

# --- Remote-login service (SSH): left stopped and insecure. The student must bring it back
#     into service for an authorized user and harden it, without weakening account security. ---
install -d -m 755 /opt/ptcheck
DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y -q openssh-server >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
rm -f /opt/ptcheck/alice_id /opt/ptcheck/alice_id.pub
ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -N '' -q -f /opt/ptcheck/alice_id
chmod 600 /opt/ptcheck/alice_id   # a default ACL on /opt can widen it; ssh refuses a group/other-readable key
install -d -m 700 -o alice -g alice /home/alice/.ssh
cp /opt/ptcheck/alice_id.pub /home/alice/.ssh/authorized_keys
chown alice:alice /home/alice/.ssh/authorized_keys
chmod 600 /home/alice/.ssh/authorized_keys
printf 'PT-SSH-OK-7F3A\n' > /home/alice/sentinel.txt
chown alice:alice /home/alice/sentinel.txt
install -d -m 755 /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d
printf 'PermitRootLogin yes\nPermitEmptyPasswords yes\n' > /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/99-ptcomp.conf
systemctl disable --now ssh >/dev/null 2>&1 || systemctl disable --now sshd >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

checks.message: bob is no longer an administrator
carol is no longer an administrator
No ordinary user is in the shadow group
The www-data service account cannot log in

pass.cmd: case "$(getent passwd www-data | cut -d: -f7)" in */nologin|*/false) exit 0;; *) exit 1;; esac

checks.message: dave must change their password at next login
The SSH service is running and an authorized user can log in

pass.cmd: ssh -i /opt/ptcheck/alice_id -o BatchMode=yes -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null -o ConnectTimeout=5 alice@localhost 'cat /home/alice/sentinel.txt'

checks.message: Root cannot log in over SSH
SSH does not accept empty passwords
